chunks: And it was narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man to whom another man says: "I buy merchandise from you on condition that you assign for me such-and-such on every cloth that I buy from you." But he is only buying for other people, and he says, "Assign for me a profit on condition that I buy from you." So he disliked it.

key_terms.أَشْتَرِي: I buy; the act of purchasing in the transaction discussed
key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: merchandise or goods being bought and sold
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: a piece of cloth; here, a unit of merchandise
key_terms.رِبْحًا: profit or gain requested in return for making the purchase
key_terms.فَكَرِهَهُ: so he disliked it; indicating the Imam’s disapproval of the arrangement

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take a commission from a seller for buying goods on behalf of others?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a transactional arrangement in which a buyer seeks a set profit or commission from a seller for purchasing goods, while in reality he is buying on behalf of others. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام expressed disapproval of this arrangement, indicating a legal concern with this form of profit-taking in trade.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (as) about a man who said to another man: "I will buy merchandise from you, provided that you give me such and such profit on each piece of cloth I purchase from you."
The man, however, buys the merchandise for others and says, "Grant me a profit because I am buying from you."
Imam (as) disliked this arrangement.
